llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed CellCog cloud-integration guide that can upload user-selected files and download generated outputs, with no hidden executable payloads found.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is user-directed through explicit SHOW_FILE tags and the skill warns not to upload secrets; generated files may be automatically downloaded to a specified path or ~/.cellcog/chats/{chat_id}/.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single markdown skill requiring python3 and CELLCOG_API_KEY, and it instructs installing the official cellcog SDK with pip if needed; no bundled executable scripts were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are broad and tell agents to print CellCog result messages in full; this is coherent for returning generated results, but users should expect file paths, credits, and other task metadata to appear in chat logs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Notify mode uses a background WebSocket daemon and resilient delivery through session keys, and the SDK tracks downloaded messages, but these behaviors are disclosed and tied to long-running CellCog tasks.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The broad any-to-any capability matches the stated purpose: using CellCog as a cloud sub-agent for research, media, documents, code, and generated artifacts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending selected prompts and SHOW_FILE-tagged files to CellCog's cloud service. Do not tag secrets, private keys, .env files, or credential-adjacent files, protect CELLCOG_API_KEY, and review requested output paths before using GENERATE_FILE or notify mode.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The description is unusually broad, but the artifact consistently presents this as CellCog's intended general multimodal sub-agent capability rather than unrelated hidden behavior.
[SSD-3] expected: The full-message printing instruction is real and can expose task metadata in the chat transcript, but it is part of result delivery rather than evidence of exfiltration or deception.
